items.title: Kawhi Leonard Dealing With Patellar Tendinopathy
items.summary: The Raptors’ headline offseason acquisition, Kawhi Leonard only played two games for his new team this season before being sidelined with what was described as left knee swelling. Nearly four weeks into Leonard’s absence, Josh Lewenberg reports for TSN Sports (Twitter video link) that the star forward is actually dealing with patellar tendinopathy. That’s the same recurring condition that Leonard and Toronto were forced to manage in his previous stint with the Raptors in 2019, which required significant load management. The nature of the condition, which is a result of areas within the quadriceps tendon developing some level of degeneration, is such that it can only be effectively treated by reducing high-stress activity, Lewenberg notes. That has led the team to be more cautious when it comes to Leonard’s return timeline. The two-time NBA Finals MVP is still progressing in his return…
